markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

No public challenges, health disclosures, or elite defections have emerged to suggest otherwise, with analysts viewing the 2027 congress as the likely venue for Xi's expected fourth term rather than any transition. Health events, acute economic shocks, or unforeseen elite realignments represent low-probability paths that could still shift the outcome before year-end.

If all three sources haven’t called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

eventMetadata.context_description: JD Vance leads the 2028 field at 25.4% as the sitting vice president, benefiting from high name recognition, Trump administration ties, and consistent leads in Republican primary polling. The Democratic side remains fragmented, with Jon Ossoff rising to 11.5% amid recent Kalshi gains and favorable head-to-head polling against GOP contenders, followed closely by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Gavin Newsom. Marco Rubio holds 10.3% on the strength of his cabinet role and primary support. Key differentiators include incumbency advantages versus legislative or statewide records, with consolidation likely hinging on early primary performance, fundraising, and endorsements in a wide-open race before major declarations.
